proposed_widenings.name: magic_item_ongoing_effect
proposed_widenings.justification: The item is a composite of passive held benefits plus an activated planted aura that persists for 10 minutes over a fixed rod location and grants area-scoped benefits while active. Current magic-item mechanics admit passive, activation, triggered_reaction, spawned_creature, and composite, but no non-spell ongoing/anchored family can honestly carry persistent area operations after activation.
proposed_widenings.evidence: As a Magic action, you can plant the haft end of the rod in the ground ... While in that Bright Light, you and your allies gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class and saving throws and can sense the location of any Invisible creature that is also in the Bright Light. The rod's head stops glowing and the effect ends after 10 minutes or when a creature takes a Magic action to pull the rod from the ground.

proposed_widenings.name: Attachment.area.origin.fixed_anchor_or_planted_item
proposed_widenings.justification: The aura originates from the rod after it is planted, not from the wielder, a target, or a point resolved only at activation time. Existing area origins cannot represent an item-anchored persistent area that remains after the user moves away.
proposed_widenings.evidence: you can plant the haft end of the rod in the ground, whereupon the rod's head sheds Bright Light in a 60-foot radius

proposed_widenings.name: DurationEndTrigger.anchor_removed_by_magic_action
proposed_widenings.justification: The aura has a deterministic early end tied to a creature taking a Magic action to remove the planted rod. Existing duration early-end triggers do not cover anchor removal.
proposed_widenings.evidence: the effect ends after 10 minutes or when a creature takes a Magic action to pull the rod from the ground

notes: The held alertness rider and held spell grants fit the existing passive magic-item surface. The blocker is the Protective Aura: it is neither a one-shot activation nor a spell-family ongoing effect, and encoding it as a direct self/area effect would misstate both the planted anchor and the ongoing area-scoped benefits.
